1485.author: VvMist247
1485.contentHtml:
As a COMPLETE nerd in regards to these books who has read each one many multiple times (seriously, feel free to quiz me if you don’t believe me), I can understand why a lot of people pick Erebus as their favorite villain. I can remember my first time reading Invasion of the Overworld. I was skeptical, I was reading it because my grandfather wanted me to read more and play Minecraft less, I wasn’t expecting much. Suddenly I was sucked into the story like GK was sucked into the game, and the first thing that sent chills down my spine was that infamous red enderman (fun fact that probably no one cares about, I wasn’t able to imagine a good high-pitched voice for Erebus until a scene in the Nether in book 2, and instead used a really low, Darth Vader sort of voice for him in my head XD). In Battle for the Nether, those dreams LITERALLY gave me chills and I just wanted more! When he killed Malacoda in Confronting the Dragon, I literally started freaking out (in a good way)!

I think what people really like about him is that Erebus set the standard for future villains. He be the OG, y’all! I have reread the first series twice now (which means i have read it a total of three times) and each time that enderman has not failed to give me the chills in the best way! Even Herobrine doesn’t make me feel the way Erebus does when I read these books!

And seriously, I would love for people to leave random GK quiz questions from any book because I have read them all multiple times. Well, I only read the Mystery of Entity303 series once, but feel free to leave questions from those books too 😀

1492.author: Madame Nova
1492.contentHtml:
That is a really good question, actually. I’ve never considered what would happen if Gameknight had never showed up or Crafter was never around.

Gameknight probably wouldn’t have been strong enough to defeat the monster kings, or even summon the army of NPCs to help. Crafter helped to glue them all together like a father and gave him the strength to keep going. Who could live without his stories?

But if Gameknight had never entered the game, the villages would probably have been destroyed, as he was the one who figured out how to allow the NPCs to bear arms and fight for justice. All would have been lost without him, and basically the User-that-is-not-a-user prophecy would never have been fulfilled.

This was a very interesting question. I don’t think I can come to a straight answer.

Ambiente: Um hacker mal-intencionado que anteriormente vítimas de cyberbullying Gameknight999 hackou Minecraft e reverteu-lo de volta para a versão 1.5.2 durante o reinado de terror de Herobrine.

Como Herobrine finalmente terminou as últimas linhas de código no bloco de comando, Gameknight irrompeu na sala.
“Herobrine. Este. Termina. AGORA! “, Gritou Gameknight, sua voz ecoando através da câmara.
“Você não é capaz de parar a minha criação. I deve falhar este programa de prisão e escapar para o mundo físico “, respondeu Herobrine em sua voz sinistra.
“Não sem uma luta”, disse Gameknight enquanto ele desembainhou sua espada.
Crafter emergiu do corredor atrás Gameknight, os dois folheados em Diamond Armour.
“Assim seja”, disse Herobrine calmamente com um sorriso horrível.
Gameknight apertou o punho da espada em chestplate de Herobrine, causando uma rachadura vertical para formar. Ele, então, com força chutou Herobrine no peito, fazendo-o bater em uma parede de obsidiana. De repente, seus olhos iluminada com um brilho perverso.
“Tente me pegar se você não pode me ver!” Gritou Herobrine enquanto bebia até as últimas gotas de uma poção de invisibilidade.
Gameknight balançou sua espada em direção a localização original da Herobrine, apenas para cortar ar. A lâmina de Herobrine seguida, entraram em confronto com a armadura de Gameknight, a peça preciosa de protecção disentigrating em pó. Herobrine em seguida, pisou nas costas de Gameknight com força excruciante.
“Crafter,” ele tossiu.
Herobrine depois, lentamente, virou a cabeça para Crafter, que estava brincando com o bloco de comando. Ele jogou respingo Poção de Fraqueza em Crafter, apenas para tê-lo desviado de volta para o seu rosto.
“Aggh!” Herobrine lamentou na dor enquanto ele lentamente passou para fora.
“Nós temos que desativá-lo antes de ele gera a criatura”, disse Gameknight.
De repente Erebus materializou atrás Gameknight. Erebus teleportados Gameknight em uma sala construída de Bedrock. Ele então se materializou ao lado Crafter e com força esmagado seu capacete em seu braço, nocauteando-o. Erebus, em seguida, colocou um bloco Redstone no topo do bloco de comando, completando a criatura. De repente, os blocos começaram a convulsão em um padrão estranho. Os blocos, em seguida, começou a crescer asas de couro, três cabeças Ender Dragão, pernas lagarto-like, e uma longa cauda. A criatura era de obsidiana preto com olhos vermelhos.
Herobrine, que tinha recuperado a consciência, olhou para a criatura em reverência.
“Estes vil NPC deve saber o que é como sobreviver em meio ao caos”, disse Herobrine com uma malícia terrível em sua voz …

By Awesomeclash11 and edited by TheRogueCloneX: The Star Wars Mod was added

Awesomeclash11 and Bladeknight23 walked up to the forest and pushed down the two levers to open the iron door. They pulled out their enchanted blades and walked through the newfound forest temple some user built.
Suddenly, there was a thump, thump, thump. “What’s that?” asked Bladeknight23 “I don’t know but it ain’t good.” replied Awesomeclash11. They marched forward to see what had made the noise. Soon, more users came in the temple. Sneakfour5, ALSkentucky1, and Enders Zheng were among many that burst into the room. “I will allow everyone to stay in this temple,” informed Gameknight.
It wasn’t long until POW!! A huge explosion rattled the room as creepers broke through the cobblestone walls and battle droids with blasters fired at the users. “Who added Star Wars mod?!” asked ALSkentucky1 “Me!” shouted Awesomeclash11 as he pulled his enchanted diamond sword while the other 4 crafted lightsabers. The fight went on as the battle droids were being destroyed.
Soon, all of them were destroyed. “Quick, follow me,” said Gameknight999. The users followed Gameknight to a village with a cobblestone wall around it. “Where are we?” asked ALSkentucky1. “A village,” replied Gameknight999. 2130.author: Michael
2130.contentHtml: Thanks a lot! Well…I’m gonna take “you scienced the heck out of this stuff” as a compliment…I like animals, especially insects and plants, and the ophiocordyceps is such a unique species with so many similarities to the mooshroom, so I figured if mooshrooms were real, that’s what they’d probably me like. It took me quite a while to come up with some of the scientific names, like Creepus Aestheticus Plantus, and Bos Taurus Ophiocordyceps Unilateralis Amanita Muscaria. I came up with them by mixing the scientific names of different animals together, like the slime being comprised of green algae, salps and pyrosomes, and the mooshroom being comprised of a cow, zombie fungus and the red-and-white mushroom. Jeez, this is the longest reply I’ve ever written!

2130.author: Michael
2130.contentHtml: Well, I tried to think of what makes these monsters unique, and then tried to figure out how they would work in real life. A few of these ideas I’ve had for a while, and my friend did actually have a pet creeper. I think the mooshroom’s description would be my favourite.

2766.author: Monkeypants_271
2766.contentHtml: This story is fantastic. The author creates a clear goal for the protagonist, but then ratchets up the tension with an initial failure. The character arc takes the protagonist on a journey of self-realization and growth that you can feel as you read. There are great references to the senses, how the main character feels while building the cathedral, which really draws the reader in, but I think the best thing about the story is the reveal of the cathedral and the mysterious character. As you read, you want to see the cathedral and you wonder who the mysterious stranger is. It become tantalizing, and I wanted to skip ahead to see them both, but I refrained from jumping ahead and just read. When you finally get to see the cathedral, it is a great, satisfying resolution, and the reveal of the mysterious character at the end is awesome. Great job on writing this graphic novel!!!!!

I changed one day. I joined a server and I helped them build, I helped them achieve their goals rather than fulfilling my own sadistic and selfish entertainment. 4082.author: adm1n
4082.contentHtml:
Whenever I am starting a new scene, the first thing I do is have the character react to the surrounds, and I choose the surrounds to reflect the character’s mood. If the hero is scared, then I choose a dark place, with lots of spooky shadows. Maybe the rustling of the leaves sounds like creatures sneaking up on him. Maybe the wind is cold and reminds him of a nightmare. Then I have the character react to the surrounding after describing what he sees with his emotions. If he’s afraid, his heart accelerates, his breathing gets shallow, he sweats . . . I try to always start a scene with sensory input whenever possible. There is a great book called the Emotional Thesaurus, which shows the sensory feelings that go with each emotion; maybe you can find parts of that online. I find it super helpful.

Mark

Pairs, April 18th, 1815 11:40 pm
The Chevotet Residence

The door creaked open slowly, melodically, almost as if it were preparing for what horrors were about to take place in that room.
The Shadow crept across the room, silently, so as to not wake the victim.
Walking over to the bed, the Shadow peered over the victim. She was quite pretty, with her long black hair, and rosy cheeks. But not even looks could stop the Shadow.
He walked over to her bedside table, picked up the water glass, and withdrew a small vial from a purse. Popping off the cap, her pour half the contents into the glass of water.
This will be the last dosage, he thought. Tomorrow morning, she’ll be dead.
The Shadow started walking back towards the door, when suddenly he heard a cry.
“Pierre?”
Pierre turned to find Emma sitting up in bed, her small form shaking.
“How could you?” she asked softly. “Why are you poisoning me?”
Pierre’s took a few steps back.
“How long were you awake?” he asked.
“The entire time,” Emma replied. “Why are you doing this to me? We’re brother and sister.”
Pierre sneered.
“Step-brother,” he corrected. “And my reason is that if you die, I will be able to inherit your fortune that your father left you. Did you know that your dear stepmother put me up to this?”
“W-what?” asked Emma, her eyes widing. “But I haven’t done anything to her-”
“Except inherit your dad’s fortune. That’s why she put me up to this scheme. I was to poison you slowly in your sleep, until you’ve passed away. Then, we were going to poison Father, and then the fortune would be ours.”
“I won’t let you,” said Emma, getting out of bed. “You’re not going to hurt Father as long as I’m alive.”
Pierre smirked, then said, “Then I suppose we need to fix that.”
Then he withdrew a knife from his little purse. Emma took a step back in horror.
“Say goodbye, Sis,” he said, then lunged at the screaming girl.

“Astella, are you ssssure thissss issss the besssst idea?” asked the spider queen. “Even the Maker Herobrine . . .”
“My father,” corrected Astella.
“Yes, well, your father, well even he couldn’t defeat The-Usssser-that-issss-not-a-Usssser.”
Astella smiled. “That’s because my father always underestimated him. But now I’m here and things will be different.”
Astella smiled again. “I personally think that girls plan better than boys. We have the skill. Boys know how to get messy when sword fighting. I say let the boys roll around in the mud, while the girls actually win.”
“But you injured about a hundred of my sssspidersssss without even a sssscratch,” said Shalkute.
“Trust me, that was only like, 1% of my powers,” said Astella. “If Herobrine created me, it’s a big duh that I’m powerful.”
Shalkute looked thoughtful. “But, do we really want to go up againsssst Gameknight?” asked the spider queen. “It’ssss impossssible to defeat him.”
“I wouldn’t say impossible. Hard, yes, but I know we can win. We just need to train first. How else do you think I’ve master all my powers? By sitting around? No. I trained. While my daddy was out and fighting with his army, I was left alone where I could practice my powers and finally was able to master them. Don’t mention this to anyone, but my dad won’t admit that I’m stronger than him. One I beat him in a match so bad, I had to carry him to his chambers myself. Which is why training an army in a crucial part in a war. But we can’t have an army without the zombies.”
“Yessss,” said the spider queen. “But . . .”
“You’re still concerned, aren’t you?” asked Astella.
The spider queen backed away, knowing the wrath of Herobrine herself.
When she was a little spider, she was part of the big army when Gameknight was at the jungle temple. She remembered Herobrine almost destroying her when she had failed to capture Gameknight. As she being one of the spider queen’s generals, she was counted on by Herobrine.
Shalkute glanced down at a scar on one of her many legs. That’s where Herobrine had got her. Shalkute glanced at Astella and lowered her head, prepared for the worst.
Astella noticed and rolled her eyes. “Okay there’s one rule we have to settle,” she said. “I’M NOT MY DAD!” she shouted.
Then she lowered her voice. “You don’t need to fear me. Think of me as your friend. A friend with the same goal.”
Astella closed her eyes. Then snapped them open again, a fierce look of anger in them. “I’ll do anything to avenge my dad, and to get revenge against Gameknight for destroying him. I don’t say this often but, GAMEKNIGHT DESERVES TO DIE!”
At this Astella pulled out her sword and swung it against the wall with so much force, that the stone blocks making it up, cracked and chipped. The sword was stuck in the wall.
Shalkute backed away even more.
Astella pulled out her sword, breathing heavily. She inspected it. It had cracked right down the middle. She put a hand over it, and moved it across the entire tool. The sword glowed with a red light for just an instant, then it faded. The crack was gone. The sword looked like it was just barley crafted, not a scratch on it.
Shalkute looked up at Astella and a look of fear came across the spider queens face. The color of Astella’s eyes had changed from blue-green to a blood red. Shalkute could literally see fire in her eyes. Astella’s hair floated on an unseen wind.
Astella looked at the cracked wall and said with vengeance, “It’s time to die, Gameknight.”

11411.author: Anti-Evil_88
11411.contentHtml:
LOVED IT!!!

I am a Minecraft Herobrine Nerd though, and so I know how he REALLY came into Minecraft… listen to this:

(This is a true story by the way that I found on Wikipedia!)

There was this man who bought Minecraft in the early stages of Alpha, 1.0
One day, he made a new world to play Minecraft on. While trying to get planks to make a Crafting Table, he suddenly saw something in the distance. His computer was horribly old, making it slow and run with a lot of lag. It had so much of that that a heavy “fog” always drifted about 28 blocks in front of him. The thing that he saw was the original Default Skin, but it had no pupils.
And it was watching him…
The user immediately checked if he had accidentally gotten onto Multiplayer, but he wasn’t. So he started moving forward, curious.
But the demonic being slowly, cautiously backed away and back into the heavy fog.
The user was able to take a snapshot of him though (which actually doesn’t make since! If I had seen Herobrine, I would have been frozen with fear! It doesn’t convince me that EVERYONE who claims to have seen Herobrine is able to “magically take a snapshot of him”!) before it left.
The user never saw Herobrine again, but strange things did happen from time to time. Pyramids of sand in the middle of the ocean, 2×2 tunnels, random redstone torches…

A while later, another dude said that it was the ghost of Notch’s dead brother. So the user emailed Notch, asking if he did in fact have or had a brother.

It took a LONG time to reply, but when he did, the answer from Notch was a very small response:
“I did once… but he’s no longer with us.”

Later, someone was able to figure out that another person had hacked Notch’s email and had sent that.

Thank you for watching this small rundown of Herobrine History.

Oh, and by the way, krazykitten2000, I wasn’t trying to basically snuff out your documentary. I loved your story! I love everyone who writes them! Please do more!

14206.author: Alora
14206.contentHtml:
Ah, so I had the idea of Oria Nightshade and Ronan Knight for a while, but I was orignally gonna have it be post-nuclear war. There would be no School, just her and Ronan trying to survive by being hire-up assassins. But, while I was trying to think up ideas for a writing contest, I thought of the book series Maximum Ride. I always had the idea for a story known as the School For Lost Children as a My Hero Academia fanfiction, while adding elements from The Promised Neverland (haha, anime nerd :P). I combined those ideas into Nightshade (as I was originally gonna call it) and transformed into the short story you now know. Truth be told, I kinda wanna explore Nightshade a little more after I write Code Luna. So, he’s a sneakpeak to Code Luna, since I don’t really have much of a sneakpeak for The School For Lost Children, since it’s in development.

In the futuristic world of New America, Code Enzume was picked out of thousands of entries to participate in the Elite Live beta test, along with his friend Julius Underwood. Talk about lucky. However, a devastating terrorist attack leaves Code unsure about himself and his past, which he has been told to keep a secret. He has three questions that still remain unanswered. One, who are the good guys? Two, who is there to trust? Three, who or what is Code Luna?

BTW, I can finally work on SFLC because after a 5 hour ACT, I’m DONE!!! Unfortunatly, Wednesday is Regional Orchestra. Cross my fingers I can sit next to my crush like last concert XD.

Wish me luck at look out for the final chapter of SFLC.

(PS If you want a sneak peak, look up the song Everybody Wants to Rule the World from the Hunger Games) Might give ya a hint on what’s coming.

14408.author: Aylah
14408.contentHtml:
Ch. 2
I looked around and saw lots of fiery bricks, and lava! I heard a pig-like grunt and when I turned around I saw a piglin running at me with a gold sword in hand. I turned around and ran as fast as I could to the edge of the great lava ocean. I then pulled out my fireworks and elytra and jumped off the cliff. I soared across the ocean and landed on a cliff in the distance. Next I found some big floating white mobs that shot flaming balls of fire. I quickly killed them not wanting to be stuck in a ring of fire. Next, I ran through some big cubes made of lava. I decided to call them magma cubes. I discovered that when I hit them they split up into smaller cubes. When I killed all the cubes the last one dropped a piece of flint. I then went on my way looking for a piece of steel in the nether fortress. When I got there I was attacked by a floating head that had rods that looked a little like french fries spinning around it. They shot flaming balls of fire like the ghasts. I decided to call them Blazes. Once I got past them I found the thing they were guarding. A treasure chest! Inside the chest there were these creepy looking eyes, and some steel! I ran to find some other treasure. In the next chest I found some diamonds and gold. I made some diamond and gold armor. In the last chest there were some more of those eyes. I ran back to my portal getting a little lost when all the sudden a bunch of blazes, ghasts, and magma cubes came out of nowhere. I fought as hard as I could until they all dissipated. I got a lot of loot and also got to the portal. I crafted a flint and steel and slapped them together to create a spark that didn’t light the portal. I tried again and It still didn’t work. That’s when I noticed that the top middle block of obsidian was missing! I then looked in my inventory for a bucket of water. Luckily I had one bucket. I went on my way looking for the lava source to pour the lava onto it. I found one of the lava falls and built up to it using the netherrack I mined a few days ago. Then I poured the water on the top and started mining the obsidian that formed. Unluckily the obsidian fell into the lava. I did this a few more times until I got enough to build a whole other portal. I ran all the way back to the portal and placed the block and lit it up with the flint and steel.

14818.author: Mark Cheverton
14818.contentHtml:
Getting published with a company requires you to first find a literary agent . . . which is very difficult. Once you have an agent, they will take your book to different publishers to see which one thinks they can put it on bookshelves and make a profit. There are numerous resources online and on youtube on how to find a literary agent, but it is very difficult. Everything rests on the quality of your writing and your story. To find an agent, you typically send what is called a Query Letter. In that email, you’ll talk about yourself and about your book and why it should be published. The agent will look at the writing in your email and decide if your style of writing will work in the marketplace. Most agents will not sign a writer who is under 18 because they have to deal with the parents, and they hate doing that, but it does happen sometimes.
When I tried to publish my first novel, called The Crystal Tear, I was rejected by 253 agents until I gave up. I tried to get the Algae Voices books published and that failed well. I’m published now only because I self-published my first Minecraft novel on Amazon and was insanely lucky. You see . . . at the time, there was only 1 other Minecraft novel, and the Minecraft players out there wanted stories. When they searched for “Minecraft Books” on Amazon, mine was usually first on the page, and I got a lot of sales. When my book made it in the Top 100 for all books on Amazon, the agent and publisher called me instead of the other way around. I was lucky.
Today, if I were to publish another Minecraft novel, it would likely go to the bottom of the list. You see, when you search for a book like “Ghosts”, Amazon puts all the books with “Ghost” in their keywords (You choose the keywords you want used for your book when you self-pub. Keywords are very important.) Amazon shows you the book in order of best selling to least selling. When you originally self-pub a book, you have ZERO sales, so you land at the bottom of the list. It is very difficult to be seen without paying for advertising.

Sorry, this is a long-winded answer, but I know you are a serious writer. I think I know how old you are, and my suggestion is for you to keep writing and hone your craft. You should read books on writing, like “Save the Cat Writes a Novel” or “Story Engineering” or “How to Write a Page Turner” or . . . Be patient and improve your writing by writing more books. Keep enrolling your books in contests and build a reputation. In college, you should try to catch the attention of an Agent by going through the Query Letter dance.

The truth about the publishing industry can be a little brutal, sorry. It’s not impossible to get published, but it’s hard.

I hope this helps. Feel free to email me through my website if you want to talk about it some more.

Mark

14999.author: Oria Nightshade (Alora)
14999.contentHtml:
So, I have a few suggestions when it comes to emotions and feelings. I’m trying to become a professional author, and have been working on make a name for myself before I turn eighteen. I find that writing emotions in third person is hard, but in my opinion, writing in first person is even worse, and that’s the POV I usually write in.

The best thing to do at first is to stop writing, close your eyes, and imagine the character’s feelings. I usually like to do this in bed XD. It’s very dark and it gives you the opportunity to fill in the darkness with the situation of your character.

For example, in my book Code Luna, my MC has many complicated emotions. I just try to imagine what my character would do, and if that doesn’t help, what I (you) would do in the situation.

The next hardest step is trying to put that feeling onto paper or on a Google Doc (or wherever you write).

First, try describing physical sensations and mix in the emotional feeling along with that. For example, in your book, you have Wonder meet Herobrine and she’s scared. However, if I met him, I’d be more sassy and sarcastic.
So I’ll give you two examples.

1 (Scared). She stumbled back, eyes wide. Inside, a churning ocean of terror started welling up inside of her, the prickling feeling of panic burning up the side of her spine.

2. I raised my eyebrows, and put my hands on my hips, a smile tugging at the corner of my lips. Though inside, I felt my flight-or-fight responses kick in, I took a calming breath and felt a matchstick of annoyance flare up inside of me. “I’m not worried about you trying to take over the world,” I say. “What I’m worried about is the fact that you were watching me without saying anything for a while. Clearly you’ve never met an angry, white girl before. We’re vicious; we go for the eyes, and although I’m not sure how you have any, I’ll still gladly claw them out.”
(Yeah, I’m an over reactor :P).

But, hopefully you get my point. I feel like I’m taking too much space here, so I’ll put everything I want to say into my quotev account. There a document called “writing advice” and I’ll put my full blurb there.

I won’t be able to update it until I get home from school, so you may not see it for a couple hours, but i’ll try to do it soon.

🙂

16924.author: Greg
16924.contentHtml:
Read the early chapters of Boys Adrift describing how boys are at a disadvantage in the first year of school for reading. Reading skills lag throughout until 12 grade where boys are years behind girls. It leads to dropouts, crime, drug use, and is a large reason why boys and men are mentally struggling.

And the common refrain is to step up, msn up, pull yourself up by your bootstraps for failing boys.

There s no positive message from school staff, policy or teachers to boys, only don’t , quit, stop misbehaving, etc.

My now high school sons struggled with rather lack of support from the school, and especially when the girls had nothing but affirmation praise and girl only pizza parties at school. My boys were dreading school and being bullied by girls who knew they didn’t face any punishment for the bullying since, no one would believe the boys.

Boys are struggling yet no one does anything except talk about it. No government programs specifically for boys, no state panel on boys, no White House panel on boys.

I had difficulty finding boy friendly books for my sons, where boys are not negatively stereotyped, made the butt of jokes, etc. basic positive boy messages, booys growing, achieving feats, and not social conditioning them to only see self worth in self sacrifice or being an ally.

The hardest lesson adds a gen x dad was finding that I had value innately and the value did not depend on what I did, my job, my money, how beautiful my wife is, etc.

Ypthose we’re all social conditioning to get me to achieve money just to support a family. Hence, the follow on of society see me as a human I only what I could provide.

That message was not passed down to my boys. They have self worth by just being born. It is the same message taught to girls by society.

My boys would get bullied by girls, kixcked, hit by girls and then told by the teacher to respect and open doors for those same girls.

The girls would plan out which boy to bully on the playground. My sons overheard them multiple times.

My youngest son read every book of yours he could and loved them.

His reading complaint was that there needed to be more books from you to red.

My older son stated that school always made him act like a girl and broke taught girl things. He wanted more school time spent on boy things, including adventure stories, with action ispnstead of always talking in the girl stories.

My observations,
Girls need to be taught to respect boys and that boys have feelings too,
Boy friendly academics need to be taught in school, for example, not turning science assignments into art projects,
Busy work should be minimized in school as it favors students who sit quietly, conform and agree. It deadens children asking open ended questions since busy work takes up all the class time. Open ended questions are not trying to show off or disrupt the class, they are asked from a genuine interest and curiosity.

Boys, my boys too, saw repeatedly favoritism for girls at school. By high school the both mostly avoided girls after years of school staff ignoring girls bullying boys

Lastly, my younger son has adhd and hated reading, Minecraft novels helped him to learn to love reading. I told him that I would pay one penny for every three pages thread. He had to read the story, even below grade level books counted, write the title, author name page count and divide it by three.

He also needed motivation to read no motivation to do math.

Divide by three is uncommon and for a fourth grader is not something he could estimate.

I know That he has read 5000 or more pages from fourth to tenth grade.

By reading, getting money to buy books, and basic math he gained confidence in school.

I didn’t know any of this beforehand. Made it up along the way.

The Boys Adrift book and the Sold a Story podcast both have it right. Reading Proficiency needs to be at grade level or above in pre k to help our boys especially and girls too.

Please feel free to use this comment without attribution or mentioning any name or identifying characteristics. Sorry about misspelling and etc, phones are not the best for long messages.

P.s. he really liked Hatchet and Holes, by other authors. He tried but gave up on the Outsiders even with many historical context discussions I had with him about the times back then.

He identified quite with books having a diary entry, self introspection thought at the beginning of a chapter. He at age ten said they were like a thing to learn for life.

My wife tried hundreds of hours and lots of fellow mom suggested ways to get son to achieve in school. I found out that shoulder to shoulder shared experience working on a common problem with a male worked.

My dad did that, I had forgotten. Work side by side and when son was ready, he would open up and talk. Therapy?

So now I read a novel, paper version, no screens, at the table when he is struggling with homework and motivation.

I started doing that when he would cry in third grade when he had three hours of homework each day. ADHD was making it take longer and longer.

Teachers piled on busy work which put adhd son further and further behind. Making his grades lower and making him believe he was a failure.

I appreciate your stories. Help our boys to read.

17195.author: Mark Cheverton
17195.contentHtml:
If you search YouTube for “Self-publishing on Amazon” you’ll find tons of videos showing how to do it. Part of Amazon’s self-publishing software is a cover-creator. You can choose images, type the title, choose the fonts and colors . . . You can even use custom images that you provide, somehow. I’m sure there are examples on YouTube showing how to do that.
But keep in mind, if you’re going to self-publish on Amazon, you’ll need your parents’ help. You must have an Amazon account with a credit card linked to it. You also have to provide some tax information because, if you sell books and are paid royalties, someone must pay income tax on it. Most kids I’ve seen self-publish their books did it under their parents’ accounts.
Also keep in mind – the minimum page count for self-publishing on Amazon is 24 pages. If you don’t have 24 pages, then you can make the font really big, add images, have huge margins, throwing in a couple blank pages . . .

Mark
